cases.sentence: На нем был ___ и плеть через плечо, так же, как у Кутузова.
cases.explain: «длинный сюртук» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: Pierre looked round. Borís Drubetskóy, brushing his knees with his hand (he had probably soiled them when he, too, had knelt before the icon), came up to him smiling. Borís was elegantly dressed, with a slightly martial touch appropriate to a campaign. He wore a long coat and like Kutúzov had a whip slung across his shoulder.

cases.sentence: А если хотите объехать позицию, то поедемте с нами: мы сейчас едем на ___.
cases.explain: «левый фланг» — after the preposition «на», the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: “This is what you must do,” said Borís. “I will do the honors of the camp to you. You will see everything best from where Count Bennigsen will be. I am in attendance on him, you know; I’ll mention it to him. But if you want to ride round the position, come along with us. We are just going to the left flank. Then when we get back, do spend the night with me and we’ll arrange a game of cards. Of course you know Dmítri Sergéevich? Those are his quarters,” and he pointed to the third house in the village of Górki.

cases.sentence: Он вот тут стоит, — он указал ___ в Горках.
cases.explain: «третий дом» — the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.

cases.sentence: — Но мне бы хотелось видеть ___; говорят, он очень силен, — сказал Пьер.
cases.explain: «правый фланг» — the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: “But I should like to see the right flank. They say it’s very strong,” said Pierre. “I should like to start from the Moskvá River and ride round the whole position.”

cases.sentence: — Ну, это после можете, а главный — ___...
cases.explain: «левый фланг» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “Well, you can do that later, but the chief thing is the left flank.”

cases.sentence: — По правде вам сказать, entre nous[668] между нами,, ___ наш Бог знает в каком положении, — сказал Борис, доверчиво понижая голос; — граф Бенигсен совсем не то предполагал.
cases.explain: «левый фланг» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “To tell you the truth, between ourselves, God only knows what state our left flank is in,” said Borís confidentially lowering his voice. “It is not at all what Count Bennigsen intended. He meant to fortify that knoll quite differently, but …” Borís shrugged his shoulders, “his Serene Highness would not have it, or someone persuaded him. You see …” but Borís did not finish, for at that moment Kaysárov, Kutúzov’s adjutant, came up to Pierre. “Ah, Paísy Sergéitch!” said Borís, addressing him with an unembarrassed smile, “I was just trying to explain our position to the count. It is amazing how his Serene Highness could so foresee the intentions of the French!”

cases.explain: «Левый фланг» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “Yes, exactly; the left flank is now extremely strong.”

cases.sentence: Несмотря на то, что Кутузов выгонял всех лишних из штаба, Борис, после перемен, произведенных Кутузовым, сумел удержаться при ___.
cases.explain: «главной квартире» — after the preposition «при», for location or topic.
cases.translation: Though Kutúzov had dismissed all unnecessary men from the staff, Borís had contrived to remain at headquarters after the changes. He had established himself with Count Bennigsen, who, like all on whom Borís had been in attendance, considered young Prince Drubetskóy an invaluable man.

cases.sentence: Граф Бенигсен, как и все люди, при которых находился Борис, считал ___ Друбецкого неоцененным человеком.
cases.explain: «молодого князя» — the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: Though Kutúzov had dismissed all unnecessary men from the staff, Borís had contrived to remain at headquarters after the changes. He had established himself with Count Bennigsen, who, like all on whom Borís had been in attendance, considered young Prince Drubetskóy an invaluable man.

cases.sentence: Теперь наступила ___ сражения, которая должна была или уничтожить Кутузова и передать власть Бенигсену, или, ежели бы даже Кутузов выиграл сражение, дать почувствовать, что всё сделано Бенигсеном.
cases.explain: «решительная минута» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: In the higher command there were two sharply defined parties: Kutúzov’s party and that of Bennigsen, the chief of staff. Borís belonged to the latter and no one else, while showing servile respect to Kutúzov, could so create an impression that the old fellow was not much good and that Bennigsen managed everything. Now the decisive moment of battle had come when Kutúzov would be destroyed and the power pass to Bennigsen, or even if Kutúzov won the battle it would be felt that everything was done by Bennigsen. In any case many great rewards would have to be given for tomorrow’s action, and new men would come to the front. So Borís was full of nervous vivacity all day.

cases.sentence: Во всяком случае за ___ должны были быть розданы большие награды и выдвинуты вперед новые люди.
cases.explain: «завтрашний день» — after the preposition «за», the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.

cases.sentence: Но еще прежде него к Кутузову подошел ___.
cases.explain: «рядовой ополченец» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “Call him to me,” said Kutúzov. An adjutant told Pierre of his Serene Highness’ wish, and Pierre went toward Kutúzov’s bench. But a militiaman got there before him. It was Dólokhov.

cases.sentence: В это время Борис, с своею придворною ловкостью, выдвинулся рядом с Пьером в близость начальства и с самым ___ и не громко, как бы продолжая начатый разговор, сказал Пьеру:
cases.explain: «естественным видом» — after the preposition «с», the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: Just then Borís, with his courtierlike adroitness, stepped up to Pierre’s side near Kutúzov and in a most natural manner, without raising his voice, said to Pierre, as though continuing an interrupted conversation:

cases.sentence: — Они, ваша светлость, готовясь к ___, к смерти, надели белые рубахи.
cases.explain: «завтрашнему дню» — after the preposition «к», the dative marks the indirect object or recipient.
cases.translation: “Preparing for tomorrow, your Serene Highness—for death—they have put on clean shirts.”

cases.sentence: — Они, ваша светлость, готовясь к завтрашнему дню, к смерти, надели ___.
cases.explain: «белые рубахи» — the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: “Preparing for tomorrow, your Serene Highness—for death—they have put on clean shirts.”

cases.sentence: — И. как это часто бывает с ___, Кутузов стал рассеянно оглядываться, как будто забыв всё, чтò ему нужно было сказать или сделать.
cases.explain: «старыми людьми» — after the preposition «с», the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: “So you want to smell gunpowder?” he said to Pierre. “Yes, it’s a pleasant smell. I have the honor to be one of your wife’s adorers. Is she well? My quarters are at your service.” And as often happens with old people, Kutúzov began looking about absentmindedly as if forgetting all he wanted to say or do.
